custodianDisclosure: No. I administered none of the reviewed controls and made no write to GitHub, Azure, or the repository. My actions were read-only: `git show`/`git cat-file`/`sha256sum` on commits 16a7e0fb, 95ee74e and 27323ec; `gh api` GETs (run metadata, environments, deployment-branch-policies, rulesets, rules, git refs); `az` GETs and lists (immutability-policy show, storage account show, role assignment list, role definition list, diagnostic-settings list); and `az storage blob download` of objects under u1/m0r6an/agent-skills/ (the shakedown decision, seal, retention-observation, retrieval-check, separation-probe, verifier-context, ledger rows, and the producer bundle, controls, toolchain and producer-identity). Those reads ran under the ambient CLI login (m0r6aN, owner, Storage Blob Data Contributor at account scope), not under u1-verifier-mi; I did not use or alter any verifier or producer credential. I used a scratch directory in the OS temp folder and deleted it afterwards. Nothing was created in the worktree. The worktree was already dirty on branch `dev` before this review and I did not touch it.
selfReviewStatement: I am the same reviewer identity that issued the §8 FINDINGS verdict (F-1..F-18), so I am re-adjudicating closure of findings I raised. I did not build, draft, provision, pin, or run any part of the closure: not the coordinator session, its subagents, the shakedown runs, the pin custodian acts, or the FK-P18-prime build. I cannot rule out that the implementing sessions ran on the same model family; I have no knowledge of their identity or outputs. This is a reviewer continuity relationship, not a builder relationship. I treated my own earlier requiredChange texts as a floor, not a ceiling, and I flag below where I now hold a closure to a higher bar than my original wording (G-5, G-6) because the original wording was satisfied only nominally.
rationale: FURTHER_FINDINGS. The closure is substantial and much of it is real. I confirmed F-1 (all 7 jobs declare `outputs:`, and run 36944407315 completed the whole pipeline), F-2 (the stored retention-observation records result `match` with both byte and document digests equal), F-9 (the store holds disjoint `runs/<id>/p01`, `verifications/<req>/a02` and `attempt-ledger/<req>` namespaces, and the second attempt did not poison itself), F-14, F-16 and F-17 (no raw `${{ }}` in any run script, no unescaped backticks), and the live ABAC role conditions and diagnostic logging. The verifier's live immutability read is real: the stored etag "8df1edb085de9a8" and state Unlocked match my own `az storage container immutability-policy show` today. It does not meet the bar "mechanism, not prose" in five places that matter. (1) The authority boundary is not enforced where it has to be. Ruleset 24258920 (the u1-verifier-pin tag ruleset) no longer exists: it is absent from the ruleset list, GET returns 404, and no rules apply to the tag ref. Environment u1-verifier still carries a `main` branch deployment policy (61546414) next to the new tag policy (61684968), so main-head code can obtain verifier OIDC credentials. `authoritative` is therefore a self-asserted label. The dossier's 'EXPLOIT-PROOF' claim holds only for honest pinned code (G-1, G-2). (2) The shakedown's INVALID is not just the F-4 gate working. Its five reason codes include U1_SUBJECT_MISMATCH, and the stored decision notes show three verifier or record defects behind it: the oracle is bound to promotionRequestId fk-p18-prime-r1 rather than the shakedown request; trustPolicyDigest sha256:c1b66138… is the byte digest of the superseded v1 pin record (commit 75d718b), and the digest it is compared to is the run-commit record (a8f986cd…); and the producer's `bundle.execution` carries 9 keys while the verifier demands exact equality with 7. The pinned producer's output cannot pass §7.4 as the verifier is written. The probe classifier also rejects a genuine Azure denial (G-3, G-4). A-U1.8.03 clause 6 says the first cycle yields INCOMPLETE/U1_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE regardless of other results; the recorded status is INVALID. (3) 'Independent derivation' is still nominal. The sandbox output is read and then ignored, and `sandbox_consumed=True` only clears the INDEPENDENCE_UNPROVEN note. Provenance confirmation proves a run exists, not that it produced the row (G-5, G-6). That is a closure that weakens the guarantee. (4) The F-19 fix changed ratified semantics without an amendment: A-U1.8.02(i) says the run executes the workflow at the pinned recorded commit, but runs now execute at a descendant (95ee74e for the dry run; the tag now sits at 27323ec) while the record names 16a7e0fb (G-9). (5) Several closure claims are contradicted by stored evidence: imageOS and imageVersion are empty strings in both producer and verifier records because the code reads IMAGEOS/IMAGEVERSION where Linux sets ImageOS/ImageVersion (G-10); the `main-pr-gate` and `agent-skills-default` bypass actor is still present although amendment A-U1.8.11 calls its removal 'due now' and a dispatch precondition (G-11); and the re-pin precondition 'actionlint clean' was substituted without ratification (G-12). A pinned verifier cannot be patched, so G-3, G-4, G-5, G-7 and G-10 each need a re-pin under standing #34. I would fix them together, not one at a time. On the known remaining gaps: the bounding is honest in naming them, but it understates two. 'Sandbox not run' hides that running it would change nothing, and 'synthetic feed' covers only part of the U1_CONTROL_FAILED / U1_SUBJECT_MISMATCH causes. The lock deferral is now properly bounded in contract text and gated. FK-P18-prime must not be dispatched on this closure.

closureByFinding.evidence: u1-verify.yml@27323ec has job-level `outputs:` on all 7 jobs (pin-check, candidate-sandbox, resolve-request, claim-attempt, verify, retention-observation, close-attempt). Run 36944407315 (headSha 95ee74e, ref u1-verifier-pin) ran every consumer with non-empty values; the store shows the ledger prefix and attempt numbers populated. The workflow file sha256 3301a0e4… matches the pin record at 16a7e0fb, 95ee74e and 27323ec. actionlint was not run (see G-12), but the dry run is direct evidence for this finding.

The decision is read back and both classes are compared: the stored retention-observation has decisionByteDigest == decisionReadBackByteDigest (sha256:5865f9f0…) and decisionDocDigest == decisionReadBackDocDigest (sha256:76c6ac0f…), result `match`; the seal inventory carries byteDigest and docDigest. The conflation self-test in pin-check is tautological (G-12); the dry-run read-back is the real evidence.

Code mechanism is as ratified: pin-check runs first, fetches the pin record by run SHA through the contents API, and the run fails PIN_DRIFT unless the ref is refs/tags/u1-verifier-pin. Event runs are non-authoritative, never ACCEPT, and skip claim-attempt. The dry run shows pinRecordReadPath api-by-sha:95ee74e and workflowRef @refs/tags/u1-verifier-pin. Not closed: the tag ruleset 24258920 is gone, so the anchor is unprotected (G-1). The `main` deployment policy remains on u1-verifier, so the authority bit is self-asserted (G-2). F-19 changed A-U1.8.02(i) without an amendment (G-9). The workflow_run lane was never exercised.

The 'observed' literal is gone. verifier-context.immutabilityObservation and the retention-observation carry a live management-plane read (Unlocked, 400d, etag "8df1edb085de9a8"), and my own read matches. The checklist gate fired on 9 unrecorded rows (U1-04, 09, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19). ACCEPT is refused while Unlocked. The lock deferral is adopted into the amendments (clause 6). Caveats: the checklist's 'recorded' rows are coordinator self-attestations (observedAt placeholders 00:00:00Z, recordDigest of a workflow file), and U1-13 still cites the superseded be3e3de3 (G-13). The shakedown outcome INVALID departs from clause 6's INCOMPLETE; the cause is G-3, not the gate.

Implemented: coordinator oracle (digest-bound), only PIN-09 gap rows admitted, exitStatus values compared, missing observedResult is a failure, minExercisedRows per invariant. Decision shows 13/13 controls absent and 5/5 invariants INCOMPLETE, so fail-closed behaviour is evidenced. Not closed: (a) the oracle is bound to one promotionRequestId (fk-p18-prime-r1) and is read at the pinned commit, so the dry-run request cannot match it and every new request needs a re-pin (G-3); (b) the classification the oracle is compared against is derived from producer-authored `observed` booleans and `demonstratedRefusalClassIds`, with requiredSignals checked as substrings of producer-authored `outputs`, and nothing independent backs them (G-5, G-6); (c) NC-U1-05..09 are verifier-side refusals recorded as producer-authored rows, so NC-U1-08 'implemented and exercised' is a claim, not an exercise.

resolve-request refuses empty or below-minimum requiredInvariantIds (INV-U1-01..05), empty promotedRefusalClassIds, and any promoted class not mapped to a required invariant (INVARIANT_OF_CLASS), before evaluation. The shakedown request carries INV-U1-01..05 and two covered classes. Read, not executed with hostile input.

Closed 15-field shape with unknown-field refusal, all-mandatory fields, `[a-z0-9-]{1,64}\Z` grammar, fetch by recorded commit SHA, IA-2.2 digest recomputed in resolve-request, verify and retention-observation, zero/multiple-match handling, and the subject-equality check unconditional. Residual issues are new findings: trustPolicyDigest is compared to the wrong record (G-3) and the request commit is not tied to protected history (G-8).

Verified live: the producer role is ABAC-limited to runs/*; u1-verifier-evidence-creator is create-only (`add/action`) limited to verifications/* and attempt-ledger/*; ledger rows are written by the verifier identity (a01/a02 in the store); diagnostic setting u1-audit ships StorageRead/Write/Delete to Log Analytics workspace u1-evidence-audit. Not closed: only 1 of the 4 denied-operation probes exists, and its classifier misfires on a real denial (G-4); the FIC custom claim template (repository_id + job_workflow_ref) is not provisioned (U1-19 unrecorded; verifier-context still records the name-only subject); the producer ABAC permits `delete` under runs/, so protection rests on the Unlocked policy; U1-09 is unrecorded. Gated by the checklist, honestly.

Store listing shows producer objects under runs/36926434897/p01/, verifier objects under verifications/u1-shakedown-2026-10-01/a02/ and ledger rows under attempt-ledger/…/. Attempt a02 ran after a01 closed, listed only its own prefixes, and did not poison itself.

seal.json exists, written last and create-only, with byte and document digests and a 5-object verifier inventory. The decision candidate is read back before sealing. The consumption semantics of the seal have a gap (G-7), but the F-10 requiredChange as written is met.

True evidenceOrigin literals (`fk-p17-committed`) and unique sandbox artifact names are in place. Not closed: the sandbox output is read into a record and never compared to anything (`sandbox_consumed=True` only suppresses the note), so §3.4.5 independent derivation is nominal (G-5). executionProvenance confirmation checks run existence plus self-asserted fields, not that the run or commit produced the row bytes (G-6). I held this to the intent of the finding, not to its wording.

Contract-side closure is complete (A-U1.8.11: P1-P3, sunset criterion, §9.2 scoping). Live state today: ruleset 22369510 main-pr-gate and ruleset 24257508 agent-skills-default both still list bypass actor 35229880 (m0r6aN) with mode `always`; required_approving_review_count is 0 and require_code_owner_review is false on both; u1-verifier has prevent_self_review=false; INCOMPLETE-U1-14 is unrecorded. A-U1.8.11 calls the main-pr-gate bypass removal 'due now' and a precondition of FK-P18-prime dispatch (G-11).

Exception is written into the amendments as a §9 assumed boundary, and the decision's limitations list cites it. The compensating records are present but two of the six values are empty strings in both the stored producer toolchain.json and the verifier-context (imageOS:"", imageVersion:""). Both workflows read os.environ['IMAGEOS'/'IMAGEVERSION']; Linux runners set `ImageOS`/`ImageVersion` (case-sensitive). A-U1.8.12 clause 3(b) requires the six values to be present (G-10).

Named gap recorded: verifier-context.attestation = {attestationIssued:false, issuer:none, gap:'INCOMPLETE-U1-18 not issued by the selected workflows'}; the decision's limitations list cites it; no code path reads attestation state. No attestation step or `attestations: write`.

Revocation procedure and record shape are in the amendments; U1-19 unrecorded refuses ACCEPT in the honest pinned code (row flagged in the shakedown). Not closed: federated subjects are still repository-name based (verifier-context, observation and seal embed the literal `repo:m0r6aN/agent-skills:environment:u1-verifier`, contradicting clause 4's 'never recorded as the trust root'); the verifier's ABAC condition allows creates only under verifications/* and attempt-ledger/*, so the verifier identity cannot write the `revocations/` records the procedure assigns to it (G-14); the gating lives in code a main-head workflow could omit (G-2).

strict_loads implements depth 16, duplicate-key and NaN/Infinity rejection; list-metadata count/size checks run before any download; evaluation exceptions are caught and still produce a decision; parse failures map to U1_ARTIFACT_INVALID / U1_EVIDENCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Read, not executed with hostile input; the dry run exercised only the happy-path parse. Residual: ledger rows are parsed with plain json.loads (minor, covered in G-13).

A grep of u1-verify.yml and u1-produce.yml finds no `${{ }}` inside any run script (only env:, with:, if:, name:, concurrency); the only backtick in the run text is inside a grammar-test string literal; promotionRequestId is validated against `^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}\Z` in every consuming job.

Ledger rows carry an IA-2.5-domain recordDigest and the -final row carries dispatchRowByteDigest/dispatchRowDocDigest; retrieval-check.digestMismatches has the {objectName, recordedDigest, observedDigest} shape (empty in the dry run, so the shape is not exercised). Live reads: allowSharedKeyAccess=false, publicAccess=false, TLS1_2, defaultAction Allow (owner decision recorded). Principals with rights above container scope that can still change the policy or re-enable shared key: two ServicePrincipals hold Contributor (059e4070… at biostack-rg, 89a63f46… at subscription) and one User holds Owner. The inventory and the shared-key detection mechanism are unrecorded (U1-09/U1-10), so the checklist gate holds.

findings.location: GitHub repo m0r6aN/agent-skills: tag ruleset 24258920 (u1-verifier-pin) and refs/tags/u1-verifier-pin; A-U1.8.16 clause 3 ('tag ruleset 24258920 unchanged'); checklist INCOMPLETE-U1-15
findings.issue: At review time `gh api repos/m0r6aN/agent-skills/rulesets?includes_parents=true` lists only agent-skills-default (24257508), main (17746056, disabled) and main-pr-gate (22369510). GET rulesets/24258920 returns 404, and `rules/branches` for the tag ref returns []. The tag ref currently points to 27323ec. With the ruleset gone, anyone with push access can move, delete or recreate `u1-verifier-pin` onto a commit whose workflow and pin record are both altered. pin-check reads the pin record at the run commit, so it passes. Environment u1-verifier's tag policy trusts the tag name alone. This is the F-3 anchor, and the closure report says the ruleset is unchanged. I cannot tell whether it was removed for the tag move and not restored, or removed on purpose; the custodian should say.
findings.requiredChange: Restore a tag ruleset on refs/tags/u1-verifier-pin (restrict update, deletion, non_fast_forward; no bypass except the named custodian), record the ruleset GET (id, bypass list, enforcement) at INCOMPLETE-U1-15, and record the tag target SHA in the pin record. Add a re-check of the ruleset GET to the dispatch preconditions. Correct the closure report line that says the ruleset is unchanged.

findings.location: GitHub environment u1-verifier deployment-branch-policies: id 61546414 (type branch, name `main`) alongside id 61684968 (tag `u1-verifier-pin`); u1-verify.yml jobs verify, retention-observation, close-attempt (`environment: u1-verifier`) on the workflow_run lane; closure report §4 'the F-4 gate made the deferral EXPLOIT-PROOF'
findings.issue: The `main` policy still lets any job running on main (the workflow_run lane executes the default-branch copy; a workflow_dispatch from main also qualifies, subject to the sole reviewer) obtain u1-verifier-mi through the environment-bound federated credential. That identity can create objects under verifications/* and attempt-ledger/*, including a seal with `authoritative:true`. Non-authoritative is therefore a label written by the same code that a main-head modification can edit; main allows a PR with 0 approvals, code-owner review off, and a bypass actor. The F-4 gate and the 'ACCEPT impossible' statement bind only honest pinned code. A forged seal is not stopped by them. My F-3 requiredChange (b) accepted labelling, but it assumed the credentials were not reachable by the unpinned code.
findings.requiredChange: Delete policy 61546414 so only the tag policy remains. Give the workflow_run signal lane no Azure login, or a separate environment and read-only identity that cannot create under verifications/*. Bind the federated credential to the tag ref and job_workflow_ref as A-U1.8.14 requires. Record the environment policy GET and the federated credential subject at INCOMPLETE-U1-15/-19. Withdraw or qualify the EXPLOIT-PROOF statement.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml verify step lines ~974-1036 (oracle and trust-policy binding), ~1192-1196 (execution equality); U1-expected-outcome-oracle.json (promotionRequestId fk-p18-prime-r1); promotion-requests/u1-shakedown-2026-10-01.json (trustPolicyDigest); U1-configuration-checklist.json (trustPolicyDigest, U1-06/U1-13 recordDigest); u1-produce.yml bundle `execution`; stored decision a02/audit/decision.json notes
findings.issue: The recorded status INVALID with U1_SUBJECT_MISMATCH is not explained by the closure report and is not the F-4 gate. The stored decision notes list three causes. (a) 'oracle promotionRequestId mismatch': the oracle is bound to `fk-p18-prime-r1`, is read at the pinned commit (so it cannot vary per request), and its digest is in the pin record, but the shakedown request is `u1-shakedown-2026-10-01`. The ratified location was per request (`promotion-requests/<id>/expected-outcome-oracle.json`), and A-U1.8.03 clause 6 requires a new request id after the lock flip, so every new request would need a re-pin. (b) 'trustPolicyDigest sha256:c1b66138… != reviewed trust-root record digest sha256:a8f986cd…': c1b66138 is the byte digest of the superseded v1 pin record (commit 75d718b, same value now in the request, the checklist top-level field and the U1-06/U1-13 recordDigest). The verifier compares it to the byte digest of the pin record at the run commit. That record embeds the checklist's byte digest, and the checklist would have to embed the record's digest: no fixed point exists. A configuration can satisfy it only because verify reads the pin record at PINNED_COMMIT (the older 5b15c9d2 version, because `pin-record.json` from pin-check is not in verify's workspace and that branch is dead code) while pin-check digests the run-commit record. Two different pin records are used in one run. (c) 'execution identity != promotion-request selection': the producer's bundle.execution has 9 keys (adds headSha and workflowRef) and the verifier requires dict equality with a 7-key projection, so the real producer output can never pass §7.4. A-U1.8.03 clause 6 says the first cycle's outcome is INCOMPLETE/U1_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE regardless of other results; the recorded status is INVALID. ACCEPT is unreachable for a conforming run, and the dry run never exercised a positive path.
findings.requiredChange: In one re-pin: make the oracle per-request (digest in the request, record at the ratified location, id check against the request) or amend the contract so a pinned oracle is request-independent; separate trust-policy identity from the pin record's own digest, so there is no hash cycle, define one pin record (read at one commit) for all comparisons, and delete the dead `pin-record.json` branch; compare execution identity on the 7 contract fields only (or amend the contract shape); re-cut the request, checklist and oracle consistently; add a negative-path dry run that shows each cause refused and a positive-path dry run (synthetic, non-authoritative if need be) that shows a fully conforming bundle reaches ACCEPT, so the verifier is shown able to ACCEPT. Reword the closure report: non-ACCEPT 'as designed' is true only for U1_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml verify step lines ~1487-1511 (separation self-probe); stored a02/evidence/separation-probe/separation-probe.json; decision note 'out-of-prefix probe denial not evidenced (unexpected error)'
findings.issue: The probe accepts a denial only if stderr contains `AuthorizationPermissionMismatch` or `AuthorizationFailure`. The stored probe shows the verifier identity was correctly denied (az prints 'You do not have the required permissions…' with the role list; observedStatus 1), but those tokens are absent from the full stderr, so the verifier raised INDEPENDENCE_UNPROVEN on a correct denial. The check used the full stderr, not the 400-char stored copy. As written, the probe can never succeed on this CLI, so ACCEPT is unreachable through it. It also covers 1 of the 4 denied-operation probes A-U1.8.07 clause 6 requires, and a write inside runs/ would create an object in the producer namespace if the ABAC were wrong.
findings.requiredChange: Classify a denial by HTTP status/ErrorCode (parse `--debug` or use the REST/SDK call so the 403 and `AuthorizationPermissionMismatch` code are observed), or accept the observed message form and document it. Record the other three probes (producer delete, producer write under verifications/, verifier overwrite) as evidence under U1-09. Probe a name that cannot collide with producer data.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml verify step lines ~1065-1088 (sandbox consumption), candidate-sandbox job lines 254-290; A-U1.8.10 clause 2; contract §3.4.5
findings.issue: 'Consumed' means the files were read into `sandbox_record` and `sandbox_consumed=True`, which only suppresses the INCOMPLETE/U1_INDEPENDENCE_UNPROVEN note. The sandbox's exit status, raw output and per-invariant results never feed t4_derive, the oracle comparison, or any comparison with producer rows. The sandbox step is `npm test … || echo $?` after `cp -r … || true`, so it produces a well-formed artifact even when the harness is missing or fails. With candidate-reexec=true, the remaining ACCEPT gates are the producer-authored rows (observed booleans, demonstratedRefusalClassIds, outputs text) checked for internal consistency against the oracle, and that is exactly the 're-reading producer rows' that §3.4.5 and A-U1.8.10 call insufficient. Reviewing the intent, not the wording: this is a closure by weakening, because the guarantee 'the affected invariants are independently derived' is replaced by 'an artifact exists'. The report's statement that the sandbox exercise 'was not run' also understates that running it would not change a verdict.
findings.requiredChange: Either implement the derivation (the sandbox emits per-invariant and per-control results in a fixed schema; the verifier compares them row by row with the producer rows and the oracle, treats a mismatch as U1_CONTROL_FAILED, and treats a missing, empty, or non-zero sandbox result as INCOMPLETE), or until it exists, never clear U1_INDEPENDENCE_UNPROVEN: the lane stays INCOMPLETE and the contract says so explicitly. Do not claim consumption in the verifier-context unless a comparison ran.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml verify step confirm_provenance lines ~1230-1279; A-U1.8.10 clause 1; producer-identity evidenceOriginPerFeed; stored controls.json executionProvenance (committed-source, artifactByteDigest e47a7816… vs stored artifact cf4d652b…)
findings.issue: executionProvenance confirmation proves only that some run (or committed file) with the claimed identifiers exists. For `github-run` it compares head_sha/event/conclusion/path/jobId against values the producer wrote, which anyone can copy from the public API; it never checks that the run is the selected producer run or an allowlisted workflow, that head_sha equals the subject commit, or that the run's artifact digest equals the row's `artifactByteDigest`. For `committed-source` it checks that a file at a commit hashes to the claimed digest, not that the row equals the content of that file; the stored controls.json (cf4d652b…) is already a re-serialisation of the committed file (e47a7816…), and the verifier does not compare rows to it. It also does not check that the commit is on protected history. A producer can fabricate row content and cite any real run or committed file. My F-11 requiredChange (confirm identities through the API) is met literally; the provenance it was meant to give (N7: laptop-generated JSON repackaged) is not excluded.
findings.requiredChange: Bind each row to its source: for github-run, require workflowRef in an allowlist, head_sha == subject commit, and artifact download (or log hash) whose bytes contain the row, compared by digest; for committed-source, fetch the cited file at the commit and require the row to equal the corresponding entry by canonical bytes, and require the commit to be an ancestor of the protected default branch. State in the contract that identity confirmation alone is not provenance.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml retention-observation lines ~1941-1961 (seal shape); A-U1.8.09 clause 3 and the §7.8 consumption rule; stored a02/seal.json
findings.issue: The seal has no `decisionStatus`, and the consumption rule refuses a seal only if retentionObservationResult != match or the decision digest does not match. The stored shakedown seal says `authoritative:true`, retentionObservationResult `match`, and its decision is INVALID. A consumer that follows 'consume only the seal' and checks the two stated conditions accepts a seal over an INVALID decision. The seal is written for every outcome, so seal presence carries no ACCEPT meaning, and FK-P19's consumption contract is untested (the dossier says so).
findings.requiredChange: Amend A-U1.8.09 so the seal carries the decision status and reason codes, and the consumer rule requires status == ACCEPT, authoritative == true, retentionObservationResult == match, a decision digest match, and an empty revocation check. Write a consumer-gate fixture with these negative cases (INVALID seal, non-authoritative seal, mismatched retention result, revoked digest) before FK-P19.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml resolve-request lines ~413-433 (gh_content at REQUEST_COMMIT_SHA), pin-check; A-U1.8.06 clause 4
findings.issue: The promotion request is fetched at whatever commit SHA the dispatcher supplies, and the verifier never checks that the commit is an ancestor of the protected default branch. The request is the coordinator-owned authority for the expected subject, invariant set, and checklist/oracle digests. The repository is public. [INFERENCE] a commit on an unmerged branch or in a fork network resolves through the contents API by SHA. A builder with write access could author a request and a matching producer run, and the only barrier is the sole environment reviewer, who is shown inputs but not content. The coordinator authority behind the request is asserted, not verified.
findings.requiredChange: In pin-check or resolve-request, require the request commit to be an ancestor of the default branch through the compare API, as pin-check already does for the pin commit, and require the path to be CODEOWNERS-covered with the P2 review settings restored. Alternatively record the request digest in a protected record (the pin or checklist) before dispatch.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml pin-check lines 138-168 (F-19 transitive binding); U1-verifier-pin.json note and `workflowCommit`; A-U1.8.02 binding clause 1(i); A-U1.8.16 clause 3 ('tag … moved to the new workflowCommit'); closure report §2
findings.issue: A-U1.8.02(i), ratified by the owner, says an authoritative decision requires that 'the run executes the workflow file at the pinned full commit SHA'. After the shakedown fix for F-19, the verifier accepts any descendant of the recorded commit with byte-identical workflow bytes. The dry run executed at 95ee74e while the record names 16a7e0fb, and the tag now sits at 27323ec, where A-U1.8.16 said the tag moves to workflowCommit. The reasoning (a record cannot embed its own commit SHA) is sound, but a change to a ratified guarantee needs an amendment and owner ratification, and the pin record's own text says 'any pin change is a contract amendment'. The closure report lists F-19 as a defect fixed, not as an amendment. The check also leans on the pin record read at the run commit, which a modified tag target can change together with the workflow (see G-1).
findings.requiredChange: Record the transitive-binding rule as amendment A-U1.8.17 with owner ratification, or restore exact-SHA semantics by recording the pin in a record committed after the workflow commit and requiring run_sha == recorded commit, with the tag at that commit. Whichever is chosen, the pin record must be fetched at an immutable commit that the tag ruleset protects, and the dossier must state the executed commit SHA for each run.

findings.location: u1-produce.yml lines ~416-417 and ~444-445; u1-verify.yml lines ~1519-1520; A-U1.8.12 clause 3(b); stored producer toolchain.json and a02/verifier-context.json
findings.issue: Both workflows read os.environ.get('IMAGEOS') and os.environ.get('IMAGEVERSION'). Linux runner environment variables are case-sensitive and GitHub sets `ImageOS` and `ImageVersion`, so both values are recorded as empty strings in the stored producer toolchain.json (imageOS:"", imageVersion:"") and in the verifier-context runnerIdentity. These are the two values my F-13 finding named as available. The INF-4 exception is justified in the decision's limitations list as 'label + ImageOS/ImageVersion level', yet neither is recorded. Nothing in the verifier fails on empty strings, so the closure criterion cannot fail either.
findings.requiredChange: Read `ImageOS` and `ImageVersion`. Make an empty value for any of the six compensating fields a U1_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE condition in the verifier, and refuse verifier-context creation when one is empty. The producer workflow is outside the pin, so correct it through a recorded builder amendment. This item rides the G-3 re-pin.

findings.location: U1-verifier-pin.json `actionlint` field; u1-verify.yml pin-check selftest-conflation (lines 182-233); A-U1.8.16 clause 2; A-U1.8.01 mechanism note
findings.issue: A-U1.8.16 clause 2 makes 'actionlint is clean' a precondition of the re-pin record; the record says 'not-available-on-ci-or-workstation' and substitutes a PyYAML parse plus an outputs wiring check, with no ratification of the substitution. actionlint is a single static binary that runs on a hosted runner, so 'not available on CI' needs a reason. Separately, the conflation 'regression test' compares a synthetic document's byte digest to its wrapper digest twice (lines 217 and 222) and cannot fail on a mistake at any real comparison site. A-U1.8.01 requires a test that fails when a byte digest is compared to a wrapper digest. The dry-run read-back match is the real evidence, not this test.
findings.requiredChange: Run actionlint in CI at the re-pin and record the result, or ratify the substitution. Replace the self-test with one that drives the real comparison function with a deliberately conflated pair and expects a refusal.

methodNotes: Method: read the dossier in full (Parts 0, A, B, C, D) and my own §8 verdict. Then read the pinned u1-verify.yml at 27323ec in full (2094 lines; the 16a7e0fb and 95ee74e copies hash identically to 3301a0e4…, matching the pin record), and u1-produce.yml by targeted grep plus the stored producer artifacts. Pin record, checklist, oracle and promotion request read from git at 27323ec; the byte digest of every pin-record version (75d718b, dc56179, 7881a60/cee585c/16a7e0f, 95ee74e, 27323ec, 9877d25) was computed, which is how c1b66138 was traced to the v1 record at 75d718b. Live state read with gh and az (see custodianDisclosure). The shakedown artifacts (decision.json with its notes, seal, retention-observation, retrieval-check, separation-probe, verifier-context, four ledger rows) were downloaded from the store and compared with the workflow code. That cross-check is what exposed G-3, G-4, G-10, and the notes that the report does not mention. Hostile-input probing was done by reasoning (empty sets, absent fields, gap rows, forged provenance, a modified main-head workflow), not by running anything. Limitations: (1) I executed no workflow and did not dispatch the workflow_run lane, so the non-authoritative lane, hostile-input parsing and positive-path ACCEPT are unobserved. (2) I did not read u1-produce.yml line by line. (3) I did not verify the contract text beyond the on-disk sha256 of the contract (8d5f849c…) and amendments (895fbe0e…), both of which match the dossier, and I did not re-check the contract's other pinned inputs PIN-01..11. (4) The tag ruleset finding (G-1) rests on the ruleset list, a 404 on id 24258920 and an empty rules list for the tag ref; if the custodian removed it temporarily, say so in the record. The fork-network SHA behaviour in G-8 is inferred. (5) I did not check that the ABAC condition's truncated tail contains nothing beyond attempt-ledger/*; I read 'revocations' as absent from the condition by grepping the exported role assignment JSON. (6) The closure report claims U1-08 and U1-18 digests; I did not recompute recordDigests of the checklist rows. How findings close: G-1 and G-2 are provisioning acts plus records; G-3, G-4, G-5, G-7 and G-10 need one re-pin with workflow changes under standing #34, plus a negative-path and a positive-path dry run; G-6, G-8, G-9, G-11, G-12, G-13 and G-14 are amendment text, records, or verifier checks that can ride the same re-pin. Re-submit for closure review the same way, with the stored decision notes included in the dossier. §8.4: I made no commits and left no files of mine in the worktree.
